faq.title: FAQ
faq.a1: Yes! The interoperability backbone is accessible at https://servicos.baita.testbeds.rnp.br/. The Management System is also operational, but access is restricted to provider managers who are part of the early-adopters program. We are currently in the acquisition phase for institutions interested in testing the solution.
faq.q2: Who is the target audience for CAFe 2.0?
faq.a2: CAFe 2.0 solutions serve students, professors, and researchers through centralized service discovery. The Benefits Portal is publicly accessible, with no institutional affiliation required to explore the available services. In addition, the Management System is designed for interaction with institution managers and federation operators.
faq.q3: What changes for those who already use CAFe today?
faq.a3: CAFe 2.0 is being developed to coexist with the current federation during the transition between federation protocols (SAML and OpenID Federation). For end users, the most visible change will be a simpler and more intuitive WAYF. For institutional IT managers and application maintainers, the new Management System simplifies the registration and maintenance of identity providers.
faq.a4: It is a digital service discovery platform available to the Brazilian academic community, accessible through institutional login. You can access the interoperability backbone at https://servicos.baita.testbeds.rnp.br/.
faq.q5: How can I contact the project?
faq.a5: You can use the subscription form below to send a message to the team, or contact us directly via email at contato.gtbaita@gmail.com. Dedicated support channels will be made available as the project advances toward production.
faq.q6: Which international initiatives are aligned with CAFe 2.0?
faq.a6: CAFe 2.0 adopts OpenID Federation 1.0, a standard being studied by eduGAIN and implemented by national federations such as those in Italy and Sweden. This positions the Brazilian federation in line with the global movement to modernize academic identity management.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: How personal data is collected, processed, and protected on this site.
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains what data we collect, why we collect it, and how we handle it. It applies to the GT-Baita website. Other services operated by GT-Baita may have their own terms and policies.
privacy.s1.title: 1. Data We Collect
privacy.s1.intro: We may collect the following data:
privacy.s1.item1: Information you provide: name, email address, institution or company, affiliation, and any message you send through our contact and newsletter forms.
privacy.s1.item2: Usage and interaction data: session recordings, clicks, navigation flows, pages visited, time spent on pages, and similar interaction data.
privacy.s1.item3: Technical information: device type, browser, operating system, approximate location, IP address, and diagnostic information.
privacy.s2.title: 2. How We Use the Data
privacy.s2.item1: Operate, maintain, and secure the site;
privacy.s2.item3: Understand how the site is used;
privacy.s2.item4: Improve existing content and develop new features;
privacy.s2.item5: Respond to messages you send us and, where you have asked for it, send you updates about GT-Baita.
privacy.s3.title: 3. Session Recording
privacy.s3.p1: We use analytics tools that may record activity on this site — including mouse movement, clicks, scrolling, and the pages you visit — to better understand how people navigate and to improve the experience.
privacy.s3.p2: These recordings are only enabled with your consent, which you can give or withdraw at any time using the controls at the bottom of this page. Although we make reasonable efforts to avoid collecting sensitive information, we recommend that you avoid submitting highly sensitive personal data through this site.
privacy.s4.title: 4. Cookies and Similar Technologies
privacy.s4.p1: We use cookies and similar technologies for two purposes: those strictly necessary for the site to function and to remember your preferences, such as your chosen language and your consent choice; and analytics cookies, which help us measure and improve how the site is used.
privacy.s4.p2: Strictly necessary technologies do not require consent. Analytics and session-recording tools are only activated after you accept them. You can also block or delete cookies through your browser settings.
privacy.s5.title: 5. Legal Basis (LGPD / GDPR)
privacy.s5.p1: We process personal data based on consent and/or legitimate interest related to operating and improving the site.
privacy.s5.p2: You may withdraw consent at any time, either through the controls at the bottom of this page or by contacting us, although doing so may affect parts of your experience on the site.
privacy.s6.title: 6. Data Sharing
privacy.s6.p1: We do not sell personal data.
privacy.s6.p2: Data may be shared with service providers such as hosting, analytics, session-recording, form-processing, and anti-spam providers that process information on our behalf under confidentiality obligations. The providers currently used on this site are:
privacy.s6.item1: Microsoft Clarity — analytics and session recording;
privacy.s6.item3: Google reCAPTCHA — protecting our forms from automated abuse;
privacy.s6.item4: Formspree — receiving and delivering messages submitted through our forms;
privacy.s6.item5: YouTube — video playback on some pages, which may set cookies when a video is played.
privacy.s7.title: 7. Data Retention and Security
privacy.s7.p1: We retain data only for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes described above or as required by law.
privacy.s7.p2: Reasonable technical and organizational measures are adopted to protect collected information.
privacy.s8.title: 8. Your Rights
privacy.s8.p1: Depending on applicable law, including LGPD and GDPR, you may have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict, object to, or request portability of your personal data.
privacy.s9.title: 9. Changes to This Policy
privacy.s9.p1: This Privacy Policy may be updated from time to time. Relevant changes may be communicated through the site or by email.
privacy.s10.title: 10. Contact
privacy.s10.p1: For privacy-related questions or requests regarding your data, contact:

solutions.card1.title: Benefits Portal
solutions.card1.description: Discover the federation's services and applications, and access everything with your institutional login. A gateway to what your institution already offers.

benefits.title: Built for the people who move the federation
benefits.description: Every audience hits a different barrier — from technical integration to service discovery. The bus solves all of them, on one shared trust infrastructure.
benefits.cta: Get in touch and find out how BAITA can help you
benefits.tab1.label: For Institutions and IT Managers
benefits.tab1.body: Integrating and maintaining identity in the federation takes a technical team and months of manual work. The bus turns that around: register your identity and service providers through guided forms, while we operate the trust infrastructure for you.
benefits.tab2.label: For Professors and Researchers
benefits.tab2.body: Federating an academic service should not require mastering SAML. The bus reduces integration to a simple registration and handles the protocol complexity, so your lab, repository or application can reach the whole academic community, not just your own institution.
benefits.tab3.label: For Students and Staff
benefits.tab3.body: Most users have no idea which services they are already entitled to. The Benefits Portal makes that visible: one place to discover and reach the federation's services with your institution's identity — from journals to collaboration tools. One less login screen, one more front door.
benefits.tab4.label: For Federation Operators
benefits.tab4.body: Today every new institution means hours of manual support and case-by-case configuration. The bus automates onboarding, metadata registration and monitoring — cutting operational load and making the federation scalable. More institutions served, with less effort per join.
earlyAdopters.case1.title: You have a service to share
earlyAdopters.case1.description: Your institution built an application, repository or tool and wants to make it available beyond its own walls. Help validate how the bus takes a service to the academic community — without today's integration bureaucracy.
earlyAdopters.case2.title: You want to modernise authentication, or have no IdP
earlyAdopters.case2.description: Whether it is a Shibboleth that has become a maintenance burden or the lack of structure to run your own IdP, help validate the bus model and offer unified login to your users.
about.p2: Our mission is to turn the federation into an ecosystem of shared services — easy to integrate with, open to discover.
about.p3: The result: more services in circulation, fewer barriers between institutions.

proposal.faq.availableAnswer: Yes. The first version is ready and registered in CAFe Expresso, RNP's test environment.
proposal.faq.infrastructureQuestion: Do we need a server or infrastructure?
proposal.faq.infrastructureAnswer: No. GT-Baita handles the server, updates, and certificates.
proposal.faq.supportAnswer: The team developing the IdP SaaS provides support, with regular meetings throughout the pilot.
proposal.faq.continuityQuestion: What happens when the project ends?
proposal.faq.continuityAnswer: The service continues after the programme, and the IdP stays on the institution's domain.
proposal.faq.effortQuestion: How much work does the institution need to do?
proposal.faq.effortAnswer: Very little: a form, a DNS record, and access to the user database. We handle the rest.
proposal.faq.timelineQuestion: How long does it take to join CAFe?
proposal.faq.timelineAnswer: The pilot has several phases: onboarding and data collection (1–2 weeks), a pilot group (2–4 weeks), and CAFe staging validation (2–4 weeks). Production follows RNP's security review. The pace is agreed with the institution.
proposal.faq.costAnswer: The pilot is a research initiative. We ask for a technical contact and feedback at regular meetings.
proposal.faq.specificQuestion: What if we have a specific requirement?
proposal.faq.specificAnswer: We design the solution with you. Unusual cases are part of what we want to validate during the pilot.
proposal.faq.databasesQuestion: Our user data is spread across several systems. Will it work?
proposal.faq.databasesAnswer: Yes. We can read the institution's LDAP/AD or host a directory populated from your existing database.
proposal.faq.systemsQuestion: Can internal systems use the same sign-in?
proposal.faq.systemsAnswer: Yes, provided they support external sign-in through OpenID Connect or SAML. We connect them after CAFe sign-in is working.
proposal.faq.experienceAnswer: Users select their institution in CAFe and sign in on a page with its name and logo, using a password and a second factor. They do not need to enter their password again for other services.
proposal.faq.mfaQuestion: How does the second factor work?
proposal.faq.mfaAnswer: Each person registers a passkey or an authenticator app on their first visit and manages their factors in “My account”. The second factor applies to all connected systems.
proposal.faq.attributesQuestion: What user data does CAFe need?
proposal.faq.attributesAnswer: Name, email, and affiliation (student, faculty, or staff), plus the student registration number for students. The Brazilian taxpayer number (CPF) and date of birth are sent only to services that require them, such as the digital signature service.
proposal.faq.dataQuestion: What happens to the institution's data?
proposal.faq.dataAnswer: A responsibility and confidentiality agreement is signed before any real data is shared. Passwords stay in your directory; we store the second factor, sessions, and access logs.
